release_notes:
Trim the right edge of the gray separator lines so it ends just inside the timestamp's right edge -- mirroring the left edge, which ends just inside the body's leftmost character. Previously the separator ran almost the full width of the log widget (widget_width - 36), so the right end overshot the timestamp column by a wide blank gap. Now the separator's right edge tracks the right-aligned tab stop tab2_x (where '[hh:mm AP]' renders) and lands 8px to the left of the timestamp's right edge -- the same 8px inset the left side already had between the separator's left edge and the body's first character. Net visual: each separator now visually 'spans' the active content region (body + timestamp) instead of bleeding out past it.

Implementation: _refresh_log_tabstop caches the computed tab2_x on self._right_tab_x; _current_separator_width returns tab2_x - 20 (= 12 window_create padx + 8 mirror-inset) when the cached value is available, falling back to the prior widget-width formula during very-early init before the first tab-stop computation runs. The existing tab-stop-change -> _refresh_separator_widths -> _current_separator_width chain re-applies the new width to every existing separator frame, so the line widths track the timestamp column as the widest body grows.
